sections.h2: Who bills tax on a Waco house?
sections.html:
Waco is in McLennan County, so McLennan Central Appraisal District sets the value, each taxing unit adopts a rate, and the McLennan County Tax Office does the billing and collecting.

Mid-2025 Census estimates give Waco 147,788 people, up 5.5% from 2020, across about 88.7 square miles. Owners hold 49.4% of homes, the median owned home is valued at $221,700 and median rent is $1,165, per the 2020 to 2024 survey. With roughly half of homes rented, many Waco owners are landlords, and a landlord's tax bill has no homestead exemption on a rental house.

A Waco address can sit inside several taxing units at once. The county's 2026 rate sheet lists McLennan County, McLennan Community College, a school district and the City of Waco, plus a Waco improvement district at $0.100000. The school unit depends on the address. Besides Waco ISD, the sheet lists Midway, Connally, La Vega, China Spring, Lorena and several other districts, so confirm which one appears on your account.

  • Values, exemptions, protests: McLennan Central Appraisal District, 315 S 26th Street, Waco.
  • Bills and payments: McLennan County Tax Office.
  • City rate and budget: the City of Waco's finance department.

sections.h2: What are the Waco property tax rates for 2026?
sections.html:
The City of Waco's 2026 rate is $0.755000 per $100 of taxable value, split into $0.578371 for operations and $0.176629 for debt service. The city's finance page describes its adopted budget for fiscal year 2026-2027 as maintaining the tax rate at 75.5000 cents.

The finance page also says the average household will see a $73.75 decrease on its property tax bill and will pay an additional $7.97 per year in utility and fee changes, as printed by the city. It lists a total operating budget of $733.3 million. Because the rate is unchanged, any change in your city bill comes from your own taxable value.

sections.h2: What is the Waco payment calendar?
sections.html:
The bill is payable on arrival and turns delinquent after January 31 of the year that follows. A weekend January 31 pushes the due date to the next regular business day, per the county.

The state's late schedule applies to Waco accounts. The collector starts a 6% penalty and 1% interest on February 1. Penalty grows monthly to 12% on July 1, while interest has no ceiling. Units that hire collection attorneys may add up to 20%. Seniors, disabled owners and disabled veterans may pay in four installments.

  • October: bills go out from the tax office.
  • November 30: first-half deadline if you split the bill under the state rule, with the balance due by the next June 30.
  • January 31: the general due date for the full amount.
  • February 1: penalty and interest begin.

sections.h2: How do I pay McLennan County property tax?
sections.html:
You can pay online with a property tax account number. Ask the tax office about in-person and mail options. The online payment site is run by an outside company, and the county asks you to direct questions about the site to the tax office rather than the county webmaster.

Card payments carry a 2.19% fee and electronic checks a $1.50 flat fee, both going to the payment vendor. Credit card payments need only the account number. An electronic check needs the account number and bank details. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and American Express are accepted.

The tax office runs tax sales online through GovEase, and bidders register there. An owner facing a sale should ask the tax office about redemption, which Texas limits by property type.

sections.h2: How do I lower a Waco appraisal or tax bill?
sections.html:
Live in the house? File for the homestead exemption. Think the value is high? Protest it. The appraisal district takes both, and most exemption applications are due before May 1.

McLennan CAD mails a notice of appraised value to owners whose market value rose at least $1,000 over the prior year. The notice lists market value, assessed value and taxable value. Market value is what the property would sell for on January 1. Assessed value reflects the homestead cap, and taxable value is what remains after exemptions.

  • Protest filing deadline: May 15, unless 30 days after mailing runs later.
  • Ways to file: by email, in person at 315 S 26th Street, or through the online portal, which the district opens for most residential property from April 10 through May 15.
  • After filing: an informal meeting with a district appraiser, and then a hearing before the appraisal review board if no settlement is reached.
  • Agents: a family member or friend can represent you if you file an appointment of agent form.

Evidence is posted in the online portal, which you reach with the property owner ID and PIN printed on the notice. The review board looks at market value, so bring sales of similar nearby homes and photos of condition problems. Homestead value growth is capped at 10% a year after the first year, and seniors or disabled owners can freeze school tax.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill if I sell in Waco?
sections.html:
A lien for the year's tax exists from January 1, so the title company settles it at closing and prorates the rest.

The January 1 owner carries the year's liability even when the sale closes in spring, and delinquent tax blocks clear title. A seller who is behind should get a balance from the tax office covering the county, city, school district and college. Heirs of a Waco home who are missing from the recorded deed can still claim the exemption with an ownership affidavit and a death certificate.

Because about half of Waco's homes are renters, a seller with a tenant should also check whether a homestead exemption was ever filed. Rental property carries no homestead exemption, so the seller's bill may be higher than neighbors' bills on owner-occupied homes.

faqs.q: What is the Waco city property tax rate?
faqs.a: $0.755000 per $100 of taxable value for 2026, split between $0.578371 for operations and $0.176629 for debt on the county's rate sheet. The city's adopted budget page keeps it at 75.5000 cents.

faqs.q: What is the Waco ISD homestead exemption?
faqs.a: On the county's 2026 sheet, Waco ISD gives $140,000 to homesteads and $200,000 to seniors and disabled owners, at a total rate of 1.034870.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty for paying Waco property tax in February?
faqs.a: Yes. A balance left after January 31 is delinquent, and February 1 brings 6% penalty plus 1% interest, with the penalty rising each month to 12% in July.

faqs.q: Can I protest my McLennan County appraisal online?
faqs.a: Yes, for most residential property. The district's portal runs April 10 to May 15, and the deadline is May 15 unless 30 days after mailing runs later.

faqs.q: Does a Waco rental house get a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The exemption needs an owner who lives there as a main residence on January 1, with no second homestead claimed elsewhere. A rental is taxed without it.
